incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT fired: service=ingest-router queue_depth=15320 threshold=10000 (rule: autoscale.queue_depth.high)
PagerDuty: PagerDuty incident INC-231234 triggered — paging schedule: eng-oncall primary -> eng-sre -> platform-leads
Amy (oncall): seeing the PD page, logs look bad. Queue depth spiking across all regions.
Jordan (oncall): Confirmed. Metrics: 1m p95 latency climbing, avg token service time steady. Autoscaler shows desired replicas climbing but actual can't keep up.
Ryan - EngSRE: Autoscaler controller logs show repeated create failures: "quota exceeded: GPUs per-project" for cloud-zone-us-west1. Might be hitting provider quota.
Maya - Platform: I'm looking at cluster quotas now. We have a pending batch resize request stuck in the controller due to IAM token refresh error (401).
Amy (oncall): Customer-impact? Claire, any active tickets?
Claire - Support: Support dashboard: three customers reporting elevated latencies and 503s on hosted API. Severity: P2 for now, but trending worse. One customer on Dedicated reported dropped inference connections.
Jordan (oncall): I'll ack PD and take lead. > `pd ack INC-231234`
Jordan (oncall): Acked. Starting mitigation checklist: 1) emergency manual scale 2) route noncritical traffic to fallback model 3) pause nightly evals 4) open cloud quota request
Maya - Platform: Manual scale blocked: cloud API returns 401 when controller tries to provision GPUs — looks like our service account token expired on the autoscaler worker. Short-term: I can mint a token and run the scale script manually.
Ryan - EngSRE: If we do manual scale, we should also drop batching windows to reduce per-instance pressure. We can push a flag to runtime: `BATCH_TARGET_MS=10` to force smaller batches.
Amy (oncall): I'm on customer comms once we stabilize. Jordan, handoff if you need.
Jordan (oncall): Taking the lead. @Maya please run manual scale to add 6 g4dn-equivalents to the pool in us-west1. Command I will run once you confirm token: ```./infra/scale.sh --zone us-west1 --count 6 --reason "incident: queue surge"```
Maya - Platform: Token minted, running now. ETA ~2m. Logs: `provision_request_id=pr-78021 status=accepted`
incident-bot: autoscaler-controller: create_nodegroup pr-78021 -> accepted by cloud provider (req 78021).
Ryan - EngSRE: While nodes spin up, adjust routing: pushing temporary policy to route 30% of traffic to smaller quantized model (low-cost fallback). This reduces pressure on worker pools. Applying now.
Jordan (oncall): Command to adjust routing: ```curl -X POST https://console.internal/redwood/routing -d '{"route": "fallback-small", "percent": 30}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"```
Maya - Platform: Manual nodes are becoming Ready. 4/6 ready. Autoscaler still reporting create errors historically but our manual tokens went through.
Amy (oncall): Noted. Claire, draft post to affected customers: short note + ETA for stabilization.
Claire - Support: Drafting now: "We're experiencing elevated request queueing; teams are scaling an internal pool and routing some requests to a fallback model. We're prioritizing production traffic and will update in 15 minutes."
incident-bot: Metric update: queue_depth falling to 8200 (was 15320) after routing change and manual nodes. Latency p95 decreasing slowly.
Jordan (oncall): Good signal. Next: disable large eval jobs that spawn persistent workers — `kubectl scale deploy/eval-runner --replicas=0 -n evals`
Ryan - EngSRE: Done. Eval runners scaled to 0. That freed ~12% of CPU in the pool.
Maya - Platform: All 6 manual nodes are Ready. Autoscaler now shows desired=60 actual=58. We still have pending pod scheduling due to instance-type affinity for GPU jobs.
Amy (oncall): Any risk of running out of spare capacity in other regions?
Maya - Platform: us-east1 still has headroom. If needed we can failover some traffic to east, but that will add latency for a few customers.
Jordan (oncall): We should leave fallback routing in place for 10 more minutes and monitor. I'll add an escalation policy: if queue_depth > 9000 again, escalate to on-call leads and exec pager.
PagerDuty: Escalation rule set: threshold 9000, window 5m. Next escalation target: platform-leads.
incident-bot: Note — autoscaler controller shows intermittent 401s around token refresh; assigning `infra-token-rotation` task to Maya.
Maya - Platform: I'll rotate the service account credentials and redeploy autoscaler auth sidecar. Doing that now.
Jordan (oncall): Also opening cloud quota ticket: https://cloud.provider/tickets/CL-99821 (submitted)
Claire - Support: Received 2 follow-ups from customers: one saw transient 502s for 45s, the other reports persistent 503s during the spike window. Both want status updates.
Amy (oncall): I'll take the external comms. Jordan, can you prepare a short incident summary for the status page? Include root cause hypothesis: auth token expiration causing autoscaler create failures leading to queue backlog.
Jordan (oncall): Will do. Draft: "Impact: increased API latencies and transient 5xx for hosted customers due to autoscaler unable to provision GPUs (service account token refresh failure) causing queue buildup. Actions: manual node provisioning, routing to fallback model, paused evals, token rotation, cloud quota request."
incident-bot: Metric update: queue_depth=4200; p95 latency trending down.
Ryan - EngSRE: Recommending follow-ups post-incident: 1) add token refresh monitoring alert 2) add quota headroom forecasting 3) autoscaler backoff retry tuning 4) runbook updates for manual-scale flow.
Maya - Platform: Token rotation done, auth sidecar redeployed. Autoscaler create calls now returning 202.
Jordan (oncall): Good. I'm going to handoff to Amy for post-incident comms. I'll remain available as second.
Amy (oncall): Taking over. Final checks: queue_depth steady <5000, fallback routing at 20% for 5 more minutes, evals paused. I'll post update and move thread to postmortem channel after we close.
Claire - Support: Notifying customers now with the drafted message.
